Quantum-Si.why: Maker of single-molecule protein sequencing instruments and consumables (Platinum Pro on the market, next-generation Proteus launching in the second quarter of 2027); its stock depends on labs and biopharma adopting protein sequencing as a biological measurement and data source, including datasets the CEO says could train AI models.
Quantum-Si.evidence: Quantum-Si Q2 FY2026 (08-13-2026): CEO - Proteus launch updated to the second quarter of 2027; more than 250 unique institutions with stated interest in Proteus; 'Proteus-generated datasets could be valuable for training models, especially when linked to outcomes or phenotypes.'

players.product: Platinum Pro single-molecule protein sequencer and Proteus platform

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the Proteus launch timeline was updated from the end of 2026 to the second quarter of 2027. The primary driver is an additional integrated instrument design cycle before moving to production (prototypes were built and tested in 2025, integrated units in the first half of 2026), meant to reduce manufacturing risk and improve system repeatability; some internal units perform above internal specifications and others at or a bit below. Program leadership and governance were changed. Management said the decision came from an internal assessment, not new customer feedback, and is hardware-focused; reagent and consumable development is largely tracking to expectations. The design, build, test and performance confirmation are expected over the remainder of 2026, carrying into the first half of 2027 toward a second-quarter launch.
quarterly_data.figure: Proteus launch moved from end of 2026 to Q2 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: no Proteus early access program has officially started; sample testing has been done for select customers. With the extra design cycle, customer sample evaluations are expected around the end of 2026 into early 2027 and early access deployments more in early 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: early access deployments expected in early 2027

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: the internal developmental sequencing kit detected 17 amino acids (reported on the first-quarter call). With the revised timeline the company now expects to launch Proteus with detection of either 19 or 20 amino acids (previously 18 for an end-of-year launch); if it launches with 19, it expects to bring on 20 during 2027, and it still expects to demonstrate all 20 in 2026. CEO: for many applications the difference between 18, 19 or 20 is marginal, but it matters for deep protein profiling such as antibodies.
quarterly_data.figure: 17 amino acids detected; launch with 19 or 20 amino acids

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Library Preparation strategy shifts from a single generic kit to a suite of application-oriented kits that can be used individually or in combination, based on learnings from Platinum customers; the company expects to bring new Library Preparation capabilities to market in connection with the Proteus launch.

Through the Platinum placement program launched in 2025 (customers use the instrument in their own labs without an upfront capital purchase), Quantum-Si worked with a biopharma customer in Europe on AAV serotyping for gene therapy: Platinum detected the relevant amino acid differences but its limited sequencing output did not reach the sensitivity required for routine use, while modelling on Platinum data suggests the requirement is achievable on Proteus. CEO cites more than 150 biotech and pharmaceutical companies developing gene therapies that use AAVs. The company says it has sufficient Platinum Pro machines and the placement program remains available; some customers prefer to wait for Proteus.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 150 biotech and pharmaceutical companies developing AAV gene therapies

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: researchers at the U.S. Naval Research Laboratory published data using Quantum-Si's single-molecule protein sequencing technology for novel pathogen and toxin detection; the company is working with multiple customers on agricultural applications, pathogen detection and typing and viral protein surveillance, has engaged multiple military and government labs on pathogen and toxin detection, and has active engagements outside the U.S. Management sizes the non-human proteomics opportunity for Proteus (pathogen research and agricultural research markets) at more than $4 billion annually, which it calls conservative, and expects some non-human markets could be early traction areas.
quarterly_data.figure: non-human proteomics opportunity more than $4 billion annually

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: more than 250 unique institutions across academic research, biopharma and industrial applications have been identified and qualified with stated interest in Proteus. CEO expects initial adopters to be a mix of early academic adopters and applied users in pathogen surveillance, agricultural, antibody production and other industrial applications.
quarterly_data.figure: more than 250 unique institutions with stated interest in Proteus

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Quantum-Si is hearing strong interest from academic institutes and biopharma in AI and rich training datasets (AI for proteomics, protein design and multi-omic integration); management believes Proteus-generated datasets could be valuable for training models, especially when linked to outcomes or phenotypes. The company applies AI internally across operations, data analysis and recognizer design.

Second-quarter 2026 revenue was $344,000 versus $591,000 in the second quarter of 2025; first-half revenue was $602,000 versus $1.4 million, reflecting limited near-term capital purchasing for Platinum, ongoing consumable utilization by the installed base, customer awareness of the anticipated Proteus launch and deliberate commercial decisions. Gross profit was $172,000 (gross margin 50%); first-half gross profit was $246,000 (gross margin 41%).
quarterly_data.figure: revenue $344,000 (vs $591,000); first half $602,000 (vs $1.4 million); gross margin 50%

quarterly_data.signal: GAAP total operating expenses were $25.8 million (second quarter of 2025: $30.5 million) and adjusted operating expenses $22.6 million ($23.8 million); first-half GAAP operating expenses were $49.9 million and adjusted $43.9 million. Net loss was $23.5 million ($28.8 million), adjusted EBITDA negative $21.2 million (negative $22.2 million) and dividend and interest income $1.7 million ($2.3 million). Cash, cash equivalents and investments in marketable securities were $169.9 million as of June 30, 2026.
quarterly_data.figure: GAAP opex $25.8 million; adjusted opex $22.6 million; net loss $23.5 million; cash and investments $169.9 million

quarterly_data.signal: Quantum-Si announced operating expense actions including a targeted reduction in force of approximately 20% of total company headcount, expected once complete to save approximately $12 million of annual operating expense; CFO expects benefits to start toward the second half of the fourth quarter, after severance-related costs, and R&D spend to stay fairly consistent with prior quarters while the Proteus program spend remains intact.
quarterly_data.figure: approximately 20% headcount reduction; approximately $12 million annual operating expense savings

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 guidance reiterated: revenue of approximately $1 million, adjusted operating expenses of $98 million or less and total cash usage of $93 million or less. With the reduction in force and other expense actions, management believes it has sufficient capital to support the updated Proteus plan and fund operations into the fourth quarter of 2028.
quarterly_data.figure: FY2026 revenue approximately $1 million; adjusted opex $98 million or less; cash usage $93 million or less; runway into the fourth quarter of 2028

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: Proteus manufacturing has been more challenging and longer than anticipated; the optical module is built by a partner, qualified and shipped to the company's instrument partner for full integration, and design-for-manufacturability changes are expected to compress the next build cycle and raise first-pass yields. Lead times for components, particularly GPUs and electronics, are watched closely and are not a constraint today; the company is procuring in advance. Platinum consumables are semiconductor chip-based and sit in the foundry world, while the Proteus consumable is a fused silica (glass) array with nanowells that many vendors can produce, so foundry-capacity exposure goes away for Proteus consumables; the instrument keeps some GPU exposure for data analysis, which the company can stockpile.
